easy.explanation: The verse begins, “I will praise thee, O LORD.”

easy.q: With what will the psalmist praise the LORD?

easy.explanation: He says, “I will be glad and rejoice in thee.”
easy.q: In whom will the psalmist be glad and rejoice?

medium.explanation: He will show forth “all thy marvellous works.”
medium.q: What will the psalmist show forth?

answers: Thanksgiving leads to rejoicing in God
medium.explanation: The psalmist praises God’s works and then rejoices and sings in Him.
medium.q: What relationship appears between thanksgiving and joy in these verses?

medium.explanation: The psalmist sings praise to the LORD, whom he calls “thou most High.”

challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes wholehearted and complete praise.
challenge.q: What does praising God with the “whole heart” suggest?

answers: Praise and singing to the LORD
challenge.explanation: The psalmist praises, shows forth, rejoices, and sings to God.
challenge.q: Which activity is repeated in meaning throughout these verses?

answers: He praises, recounts, rejoices, and sings
challenge.explanation: These verses present a sequence of praise, testimony, rejoicing, and song.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence of the psalmist’s actions?

paragraphs.title: God's Judgment and the Fall of the Enemies

answers: They turn back, fall, and perish
easy.explanation: The verse says, “When mine enemies are turned back, they shall fall and perish.”
easy.q: What happens to the psalmist’s enemies?

easy.explanation: The LORD sits on the throne “judging right” and judges “in righteousness.”
The text says, “The LORD shall endure for ever.”
easy.q: How long will the LORD endure?

answers: The LORD maintains the psalmist’s right and cause
medium.explanation: The psalmist connects their defeat with God’s judgment on his behalf.
medium.q: Why do the enemies fall and perish?

medium.explanation: In context, uprightness describes just and fair judgment.
medium.q: What does “uprightness” mean in the statement that God ministers judgment in uprightness?

answers: The enemies perish, but the LORD endures for ever
The enemies judge, but the LORD flees
The enemies build, but the LORD disappears
medium.explanation: The enemies are destroyed, while the LORD remains forever.
medium.q: What contrast is made between the enemies and the LORD?

challenge.explanation: The LORD has prepared His throne for judgment.
challenge.q: What does the LORD’s throne reveal about His rule?

answers: They retreat, fall, perish, and are destroyed
challenge.explanation: The passage describes their turning back, falling, perishing, and destruction.
challenge.q: What progression is described concerning the enemies?

challenge.explanation: God judges “the world” and ministers judgment to “the people.”
challenge.q: What is the scope of God’s judgment in these verses?

paragraphs.title: God as Refuge for the Afflicted and Proclaiming His Deeds

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The LORD also will be a refuge for the oppressed.”
easy.q: For whom is the LORD a refuge?

easy.explanation: The LORD has not forsaken “them that seek thee.”
easy.q: Whom has the LORD not forsaken?

easy.explanation: They are told to “declare among the people his doings.”
easy.q: What are God’s people told to declare among the people?

answers: So he may show forth God’s praise and rejoice in salvation
So he may rule the nations
medium.explanation: He asks for mercy and deliverance so that he may praise God and rejoice.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask the LORD for mercy?

medium.explanation: The word describes a place of safety and protection during trouble.
medium.q: What does “refuge” mean in “a refuge in times of trouble”?

answers: Deliverance enables the psalmist to declare God’s praise
Mercy prevents the psalmist from singing
medium.explanation: The psalmist asks for mercy so he can show forth all God’s praise.
medium.q: How are mercy and praise connected in these verses?

challenge.explanation: The verse says, “they that know thy name will put their trust in thee.”
challenge.q: What should those who know the LORD’s name do?

answers: God’s people in Zion are to declare His deeds among the nations
The nations are commanded to destroy Zion
challenge.explanation: Those who dwell in Zion are told to declare God’s doings among the people.
challenge.q: What connection is made between Zion and the nations?

answers: Have mercy, consider his trouble, and lift him from death
challenge.explanation: He asks God to have mercy, consider his trouble, and lift him from the gates of death.
challenge.q: What does the psalmist ask God to do before he praises Him?

paragraphs.title: The Wicked Caught by Their Own Deeds

easy.explanation: The heathen are sunk down “in the pit that they made.”
easy.q: Where are the heathen sunk down?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “in the net which they hid is their own foot taken.”
easy.q: Whose foot is taken in the hidden net?

easy.explanation: The text says, “The wicked shall be turned into hell.”
easy.q: Where shall the wicked be turned?

answers: People can be trapped by the snares they prepare
medium.explanation: The heathen are caught in the pit and net they made and hid.
medium.q: What principle is shown by the pit and net?

medium.explanation: To be snared means to be caught in a trap.
medium.q: What does “snared” mean in the phrase “the wicked is snared in the work of his own hands”?

answers: The wicked are caught by their own works and turned into hell
medium.explanation: The passage presents judgment through self-made traps and punishment.
medium.q: How is God’s judgment shown in these verses?

answers: The wicked’s own deeds contribute to their downfall
The wicked’s deeds do not matter
The wicked are saved by their deeds
challenge.explanation: The wicked are trapped in the consequences of what they themselves have done.
challenge.q: What is the significance of the phrase “the work of his own hands”?

answers: The nations that forget God go to hell, while the needy are not forgotten
The needy go to hell while the nations are saved
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts the fate of those who forget God with God’s care for the needy.
challenge.q: What difference is shown between the nations that forget God and the needy?

answers: God’s actions in judgment reveal who He is
God does not act in judgment
Human beings alone carry out judgment
challenge.explanation: God is made known through the judgment He performs.
challenge.q: What does “The LORD is known by the judgment which he executeth” mean?

paragraphs.title: The Hope of the Poor and a Prayer for God's Revelation

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the needy shall not alway be forgotten.”
easy.q: Who shall not always be forgotten?

easy.explanation: The expectation of the poor “shall not perish for ever.”
easy.q: What shall not perish for ever?

easy.explanation: He cries, “Arise, O LORD,” and asks that the heathen be judged.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do?

answers: So they may know that they are only men
medium.explanation: The purpose is that the nations may know themselves to be but men.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask the LORD to put the nations in fear?

medium.explanation: The request is for the nations to experience fear before God.
medium.q: What does “fear” mean in “Put them in fear, O LORD”?

answers: God’s judgment protects the hope of the poor
medium.explanation: The psalmist asks God to act because the needy should not be forgotten.
medium.q: How are the hope of the poor and the request for judgment connected?

answers: Human beings must not have unlimited power before God
Human beings should become stronger than God
challenge.explanation: The request emphasizes human limitation before God’s authority.
challenge.q: What does “let not man prevail” mean in context?

answers: Human power is limited, while God judges the nations
Man judges God, while the nations are saved
The poor are forgotten, while the wicked are preserved
challenge.explanation: The ending places limited humanity under God’s righteous judgment.
challenge.q: What contrast appears at the end of the psalm?

answers: To make them recognize the limits of their power
To give them rule over the world
To make them forget the LORD
challenge.explanation: The psalmist asks that the nations recognize their human limitations.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of reminding the nations that they are men?
